# MIDI and menu scenario fixture correction

Exact starting index tree: `0260cd3f78a1b3717ef988d54aca767d65b6a2bb` (unchanged index). Only eight scenario files changed, unstaged; no production or runner edits.

All eight selectors reproduced FAIL before edits (runner exit 1), matching the saved candidate receipts; all eight passed on exact base c295af1554f9e80a29864cd013995eccad66cd2c. This task reused the baseline receipts and did not rerun the baseline.

The GLOBAL category index now needs explicit SEL entry into MIDI + CLOCK; HOME returns to the category index before closing GLOBAL. Clock setup, stored bytes, transport, probability and note-count expectations were retained. PROJECT is located before SYSTEM by saturating SELECT then moving back one, so the tour does not depend on whether the BLUETOOTH category exists. RESET is PROJECT row 4.

Arrows: > enters a category and consumes the held press; < returns to the category index. The fixtures now explicitly exercise those transitions and re-enter the remembered section row. ALGO decrements values in GLOBAL, while existing page-list two-way arrow edit checks are retained. The shorter navigation event total is 70/71/73/75 rather than 110/111/113/115 because held < section exits no longer repeatedly edit values; the +1 tap/+2 hold/no-route increments remain asserted. Clip-mode same-frame category entry remains covered, followed by a frame-observed release (50 ms) and a new value-edit press. The original immediate and later clock-value assertions are retained.

Assertion audit confirms every original functional `expect` remains with at least its original multiplicity, excluding only genuinely changed `listsel` and `arrowsteps` navigation assertions. No assertions were weakened to inequalities and no clock, note, probability, storage, tempo or value endpoint expectation changed.

Run results: before eight FAIL, exit 1. First correction: six PASS; only arrows and clip-arrow-menu remained FAIL, exit 1. After fixing navigation counters and release observation, those two PASS, exit 0. One final assertion-only change restored the immediate clip clock assertion, then only clip-arrow-menu reran and PASS, exit 0. Six passing selectors were not rerun. `results.json` has exact commands/exits; before/after logs are preserved.

Latest combined scoped result: all eight assigned selectors PASS. Full suite/native/device qualification NOT_RUN. Patch is incremental `git diff` against the exact starting index; no staging or commit was performed.

# Storage/performance scenario fixture fix

Exact starting index tree: `0260cd3f78a1b3717ef988d54aca767d65b6a2bb` (still unchanged). Source base: `c295af1554f9e80a29864cd013995eccad66cd2c`.

Seven test scenario files only. No production files, runner changes, staging or commit. Incremental patch is `../storage.patch`, SHA-256 `e2128c1aeffd3df7472bc8f2a503af4f38d17ec57ee22191667d411c65128f24`.

Before: all eight assigned selectors reproduced FAIL, runner exit 1. After: all eight PASS, runner exit 0. Existing matching c295af baseline receipts show all eight PASS; reused without rerunning baseline. Both runs used:

```sh
sh tests/run_tests.sh scenario-autosave scenario-guard scenario-migrate scenario-migrate0102 scenario-perf scenario-perfsave scenario-undo perf-scratch
```

Root cause: stale flat-GLOBAL navigation never entered the new PROJECT/SYSTEM sections. The edits select the final SYSTEM category or preceding PROJECT category, enter it, and select the original target row. `turn SELECT 6` saturates the current five- or six-category list; this avoids a board-dependent category index. PROJECT AUTOSAVE is row 2, RESET is row 4; SYSTEM PERFORMANCE is row 0. Semantic section positions are verified from ui.c:1549–1601. Actual execution here uses the default host configuration; an additional SMK variant was not run.

All existing reset confirmation, unsupported-store rejection, autosave persistence, undo, performance, guard, save and audio comparison assertions remain. Only obsolete menu-row assertions were replaced with current section-row assertions. Migration fixtures continue to reject old revisions; no migration behavior was added. `perf-scratch` now reaches its existing scratch compilation and WAV byte comparison and passes; no runner edits were needed.

The runner's package note remains skipped (missing native app/loader/SDK). No full unfiltered suite, native, package or device claim. See before/after logs, per-selector logs, exact exits and results.json. Parent owns integration/review of the incremental test patch.
